The bilayer cloak consists of an inner layer made of a perfect electric conductor (PEC) or metal, and an outer layer with a specific dielectric constant.
The required dielectric constant for the outer layer of the bilayer cloak is given by the equation ε₂ = (c²/b² - 1)/(ε₂/ε₁ - 1).

The fabricated bilayer cloak used a steel tube with inner radius of 1.3 cm and outer radius of 1.5 cm as the inner layer, and a photosensitive resin shell container with inner radius of 1.5 cm and outer radius of 1.95 cm as the outer layer.
Simulations and experiments showed that the bilayer cloak was able to guide the electric field around the shielded region without any disturbance, achieving a uniform electric field distribution.
The carpet cloak design used a transformation that stretched the region AOB to AC'B, while keeping ACB unchanged.
The carpet cloak was fabricated using a metamaterial structure composed of alternating layers of air (ε_r = 1.0) and ultrapure water (ε_r = 80.0).
Simulations and experiments showed that the carpet cloak was able to guide the electric field around the shielded region without any distortion, restoring a uniform electric field distribution.
The electrostatic cloaks can be readily fabricated using naturally occurring materials and have a simple structure that is scalable to micro/nanoscale and 3D configurations.
The bilayer cloak only works for inhomogeneous electric fields and may have poor performance for point source fields.
The carpet cloak requires anisotropic metamaterials which can be more challenging to fabricate.
The concepts demonstrated in this paper can be extended to develop other devices such as concentrators, rotators, and illusions for various applications.
Achieving perfect cloaking for electrostatic fields is easier compared to the challenges faced by electromagnetic wave cloaks.
The bilayer cloak design is based on cancelling technology, while the carpet cloak design is based on transformation optics.
The rotation angle between the new and original coordinate systems for the carpet cloak is given by θ = arctan(2τ/(k²+τ²-1)).
The required dielectric constant tensor components for the carpet cloak are ε_x'x' = (k²+τ²+1)-(k²+τ²-1)²+4τ²/2k and ε_y'y' = (k²+τ²+1)+(k²+τ²-1)²+4τ²/2k.
